title: Plan a Deferred-Sharing Maintenance Window
summary: Write an operational runbook for a large access-model change, including the distinct steps of resuming calculations and recalculating accumulated changes.
prerequisites: Understand sharing rules, groups, ownership, and effective-access tests.
Complete S10 and S11 or equivalent access-model work.
learningObjectives: Explain what sharing-rule deferral does and does not pause.
Design a maintenance sequence with verification gates.
Separate a tabletop rehearsal from an authorized production operation.

sections.heading: Deferral changes timing, not the intended access policy
body: Northstar is reorganizing dealer groups and roles. Recalculating sharing rules after every individual change may create unnecessary repeated work. Sharing-rule deferral can temporarily suspend relevant automatic calculations while a planned set of changes is made. The target access policy remains the business requirement; deferral is an operational timing mechanism.

Availability matters. The feature is not enabled by default in every org, and Salesforce documentation describes contacting Support to enable it. The operator also needs the relevant permissions. This classroom exercise does not ask you to enable the feature, reorganize a real role hierarchy, or assume that a Developer Edition can reproduce a large maintenance event.

callouts.text: A runbook describes a controlled operation with owners, checkpoints, and recovery decisions. It is more than a list of buttons.

sections.heading: Know exactly what is paused
body: Deferring sharing-rule calculations does not freeze every sharing-related mechanism. Manual shares and changes involving teams or queues can still be evaluated. Some role changes matter to sharing rules while other changes do not fall under the same deferral. Group-membership calculations have their own considerations; do not collapse all these mechanisms into a single 'security off' switch.

Existing record access can temporarily differ from the intended final configuration while changes await recalculation. This creates a business and access-management risk, not simply a performance benefit. Define which users and operations may continue during the window, how unexpected visibility will be handled, and who can stop the procedure.

The synthetic window below is a rehearsal timeline. Its times organize discussion and do not predict how long Salesforce will take to recalculate a real org. A real duration depends on the organization's data, access structure, concurrent activity, and platform behavior.

callouts.text: Do not claim that deferral disables permission checks or makes all access changes wait until Resume.

codeBlocks.caption: Synthetic maintenance rehearsal
codeBlocks.code:
T0: record current configuration and expected persona matrix
T1: confirm approved scope, operator, recovery owner, and available window
T2: suspend relevant sharing-rule calculations
T3: apply reviewed group/role changes
T4: resume automatic calculations for new changes
T5: request full sharing-rule recalculation for accumulated changes
T6: wait for completion and verify allowed/denied access
T7: close only after evidence and ownership checks pass

sections.heading: Resume and Recalculate are different gates
body: Resume re-enables automatic handling of new changes. It does not replace the required full recalculation for changes accumulated during suspension. If the operator stops after Resume, the configuration may look finished while record access still reflects stale calculations. The runbook must therefore have two separate completion checks.

After requesting recalculation, monitor the supported status signals and wait for the relevant work to complete before declaring success. Then execute the persona matrix: Anna's East appointments, Max's West appointments, Oleg's managerial view, and explicitly denied cross-dealer cases. Include exceptions that should have expired.

Do not assume that reverting a role or group definition instantly reverses every consequence of an interrupted operation. Recovery may require restoring configuration, resuming work, recalculating, and verifying access again. Decide who can authorize each step and what evidence supports the decision.

callouts.text: The maintenance window is not complete when the last configuration edit is saved; it is complete when the final access state is verified.

sections.heading: Prepare a useful rehearsal
body: Create three tabletop failure cards: the change list is only partially applied, the operator resumes but forgets recalculation, and a manual share is added during the window. For each, explain the expected uncertainty and the next safe decision. Avoid inventing automatic rollback guarantees.

Measure the operation through checkpoint timestamps, configuration counts, recalculation status, verification coverage, and unresolved exceptions. In a real approved environment these become observations. In this lesson they remain a plan unless you perform a separately authorized small test.

A good runbook includes a short communication message for Oleg, the business owner: which users may notice changes, what is temporarily restricted, what defines completion, and how to report unexpected access. Keep technical console details in the operator section so the business message stays understandable.

callouts.text: Assign a named role to every gate: operator, access verifier, business owner, and recovery decision-maker.

exercise.title: Rehearse a dealer-group reorganization
exercise.brief: Prepare a runbook and three failure-card responses for a synthetic Northstar access change.
steps: List the approved configuration changes and capture a proposed before/after access matrix.
Define prerequisites, feature availability checks, permissions, owners, and stop conditions.
Write Suspend, change, Resume, Recalculate, completion monitoring, and verification as separate steps.
Work through the three failure cards and state what must be verified before resuming normal use.
Add an evidence checklist and a short business communication draft; do not run the maintenance operation.
acceptance: Resume and full Recalculate are explicit separate requirements.
The plan acknowledges mechanisms that are not paused by sharing-rule deferral.
Completion requires verified access and resolved exceptions, not only saved configuration.
exercise.stretch: Explain how you would coordinate unrelated group-membership work during the same window.

knowledgeCheck.question: What remains unfinished after Resume alone?
knowledgeCheck.answer: The changes accumulated while sharing-rule calculations were suspended still require the documented full recalculation.

knowledgeCheck.question: Are manual shares necessarily delayed by this deferral?
knowledgeCheck.answer: No. Sharing-rule deferral does not pause every sharing mechanism; manual shares are among the changes evaluated separately.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why rehearse recovery?
knowledgeCheck.answer: An interrupted access change can leave configuration and effective access out of sync. Recovery needs a decision sequence and verification, not an assumed instant undo.

recap: Deferral is a controlled scheduling procedure.
Close the window on verified access, not on operator optimism.
